p2.title: Keycloak v11.0.0 update and ear packaging module add

p14.title: FM2-403: Add Launch Type in Redirect URl

nodes.body: @ibacher @VaishSiddharth Added LaunchType parameter in redirect URL. PTAL

So, a request can have multiple launch types, e.g., `launch/user, launch/encounter, launch/patient` all in one go. It seems that rather than trying to pass this as a parameter, we just need to return whatever information we have a have logic here to decide which fields to populate.

Also, data passed from Keycloak to OMRS should *always* be in a token rather than in a URL parameter. This is, for example, how we pass the user to OMRS. The reason for doing this is that the token is signed by Keycloak, so we can be sure that the parameter was provided by Keycloak rather than a user. We should likely have a similar setup in the smartonfhir module when we're passing parameters around, but that's another step towards productionising this.
@ibacher, thanks. Please correct me if I understood wrong. Do we need to pass the launchType (i.e., "encounter" or "patient") parameter in token securely?

So two things:

1. Yes, if we are passing the launch type, it needs to be in the token
2. But, how are we going to address a request for multiple launch parameters? This can probably be handled either by multiple challenge steps in the authenticator or handled inside OMRS.

@ibacher I think handling it into the authenticator will be better because if we do this here, we only need to check the launchType in OMRS. 

So currently, we only support patient and encounter standalone launches. if the client request only for patient context (scope contain launch/patient but not launch/encounter) then we set the `launchType="patient"` but if client request for encounter context (scope contains both launch/patient and launch/encounter) then we set the `launchType="encounter"`.  By Checking the scope requested, we can easily predict the launchType. Thought?
I don't quite get why this was changed?

Actually, we have changed the same logic to `map` in our last commit [here](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-keycloak-smart-auth/blob/5697511aac2e3da364f44051750d089ebe51d731/openmrs-keycloak-smart-auth/src/main/java/org/openmrs/contrib/keycloak/smart/auth/provider/SmartLaunchAccessAuthenticator.java#L175).

Again, the idea with putting things in the token is that the token is signed and therefore we can verify that it was generated by Keycloak whereas a query parameter could be populated by a malicious user (this is a security context, so we have to be careful about security).
@ibacher thanks, I will change this and put the `launchType` parameter into token.

p21.title: FM2-690: Bump the SMART auth SPI to Keycloak 26
p21.body:
## Description of what I changed

Ports the plugin from **Keycloak 14.0.0 to 26.7.1**. That is twelve major versions, and it crosses the
point where Keycloak stopped being a WildFly application and became a Quarkus one, so most of the diff is
what that move forces.

**The dependencies.** Same four artifacts — `keycloak-core`, `keycloak-server-spi`, `keycloak-services`,
`keycloak-server-spi-private` — now on one `${keycloak.version}` property rather than four literals. It is
**pinned, not floated**: every SPI here is one Keycloak marks internal and logs `KC-SERVICES0047` for, so a
minor bump can change any of them with no compiler warning.

**`javax.*` → `jakarta.*`.** Keycloak 17 moved to Quarkus and with it to Jakarta EE, so every
`javax.ws.rs.core.Response` import becomes `jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response`. Touches every provider that
returns a `Response`.

**A changed Keycloak API.** `UserProvider.getUserByUsername` flipped its argument order between 14 and 26:
`getUserByUsername(username, realm)` is now `getUserByUsername(realm, username)`. Both call sites updated.

**The WildFly EAR is gone.** Keycloak 26 loads providers from `providers/` as plain jars and builds them in
with `kc.sh build` — there is no application server left to deploy an EAR into. So `openmrs-keycloak-ear`
and its `jboss-deployment-structure.xml` are deleted (61 lines) and `wildfly-maven-plugin` goes with them.
The surviving module is renamed `openmrs-keycloak-smart-auth` → `keycloak-smart-auth`, and the parent
artifactId `openmrs-keycloak-smart-authentication` → `keycloak-smart-auth-parent`.

**Keycloak's own provider registration changed.** In 26.7.1 the built-in `UsernamePasswordForm` is offered
only as `REQUIRED`, so it can no longer sit as an `ALTERNATIVE` in a flow. `AlternativeUsernamePasswordFormFactory`
subclasses it and re-registers it under its own id, which is what lets the SMART launch and the password
form be alternatives to each other.

**The EHR launch no longer mints an action token.** An action token has to name a user, and an EHR launch
has nobody authenticated yet — the old code satisfied that by looking up the literal username `admin`,
which does not exist on a stock OpenMRS database, where the administrator's `username` column is NULL and
`admin` is its `system_id`. The EHR path now hands OpenMRS an ordinary action URL and takes the clinician
from the subject of the signed token OpenMRS returns. `SmartLaunchAccessActionToken` and its handler are
deleted with the path that produced them; the standalone launch still uses an action token and still has
one handler registered. A returned username the realm has no user for now leaves the launch to the next
authenticator, rather than completing an execution with nobody authenticated and landing the clinician on
Keycloak's `UNKNOWN_USER` page.

**Java 8 → 17**, which is Keycloak 26's floor:

- `<source>8</source><target>8</target>` → `<release>17</release>`
- JaCoCo `0.8.5` → `0.8.12`; 0.8.5 cannot read class file major version 61
- Surefire `3.0.0-M4` → `3.5.2`
- JUnit `4.13.1` → JUnit `5.11.4` via `junit-bom`, and Mockito `5.14.2` with `mockito-junit-jupiter`

**CI.** The matrix was `[8, 10, 11, 12, 13]`, so with `maven.compiler.release=17` every job failed with
`release version 17 not supported` — the whole matrix was red for a reason unrelated to any change. It is
now `[17, 21]`: 17 is the bytecode target, 21 is what Keycloak 26 actually runs on, and both have to pass.
Also switched to the shared `openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows` `build-maven.yml` — this is a plain provider jar,
not an omod, so `build-backend-module.yml` was the wrong workflow — and added `workflow_dispatch`.

**A required `aud` validator for SMART 2.x.** Without it a token minted for one FHIR server is replayable
against another trusting the same realm. It fails closed: unconfigured, or with no audience presented, it
rejects. Which client note carries that audience depends on whether Keycloak recognises the parameter —
`aud` and `audience` are unknown to it and arrive under the `client_request_param_` prefix, while `resource`
is one of its own and arrives as a plain note under that name — so the validator reads both spellings for
every parameter it accepts.

**This plugin's first test suite**, 131 tests. Besides the behaviour, they pin the constraints Keycloak
enforces at realm-import or startup rather than at compile time: provider ids inside the `VARCHAR(36)`
column that stores them, ids that do not shadow a built-in authenticator, a services file that names no
class the jar lacks and none registered under the wrong SPI, and no factory in the jar that the services
file fails to name. `UPGRADING.md` records which of these couplings can break silently on the next bump,
and how to verify each.

**One breaking config change.** The five authenticator config keys are renamed from kebab-case to
snake_case: `smart-launch-secret-key` → `smart_launch_secret_key`, `smart-launch-supported-params` →
`smart_launch_supported_params`, `smart-patient-selection-url` → `smart_patient_selection_url`,
`smart-launch-access-url` → `smart_launch_access_url`, `smart-launch-access-secret-key` →
`smart_launch_access_secret_key`. Keycloak stores whatever key it is given and ignores what a provider
does not read, so a realm still carrying the old spellings imports cleanly and then reads a null secret:
every launch fails with *"Secret key is not configured for realm ..."*. Any realm predating this PR needs
its `authenticatorConfig` keys updated along with the jar. The paired realm in
openmrs-distro-smartonfhir already uses the new spellings.

### Trying this out

This plugin does not produce a working launch on its own — the realm, the chart affordance and an actual
SMART application all live outside it. Three repositories exist for that, and none of them is proposed
for upstream; they are demonstration and integration scaffolding:

| Repository | What it is |
|---|---|
| [openmrs-distro-smartonfhir](https://github.com/mherman22/openmrs-distro-smartonfhir) | A compose stack: Reference Application 3.7.1 with Keycloak 26.7.1, and the realm itself — the authentication flow, the client, the SMART scopes and the claim mappers. A jar Keycloak has loaded but never invokes is invisible, so this is what makes the providers reachable. |
| [openmrs-esm-smart-app-launch-app](https://github.com/mherman22/openmrs-esm-smart-app-launch-app) | The O3 frontend module: **Launch an app** in the patient chart's Actions menu, and the patient-selection screen a standalone launch needs. |
| [openmrs-smart-vitals-reviews-app](https://github.com/mherman22/openmrs-smart-vitals-reviews-app) | A real SMART application that reads the launched patient over FHIR — trends their vitals, derives a BMI the server does not store. Published as an image, so the distro pulls it rather than building it. |

```bash
for repo in openmrs-distro-smartonfhir openmrs-module-smartonfhir \
            openmrs-contrib-keycloak-smart-auth openmrs-contrib-keycloak-auth \
            openmrs-esm-smart-app-launch-app; do
  git clone https://github.com/mherman22/$repo.git
done

(cd openmrs-module-smartonfhir          && mvn clean install)   # the OpenMRS module
(cd openmrs-contrib-keycloak-smart-auth && mvn clean install)   # Keycloak's SMART extensions
(cd openmrs-contrib-keycloak-auth       && mvn clean install)   # OpenMRS users as Keycloak's user store

cd openmrs-distro-smartonfhir
cp .env.example .env        # then set SMART_LAUNCH_SECRET, e.g. openssl rand -base64 32
docker compose up -d --build
```

Then open **http://localhost/openmrs/spa**, sign in, open a patient, and choose **Launch an app** from
the Actions menu. Maven needs JDK 17 or newer; the first run installs the OpenMRS database and assembles
the frontend, so it takes several minutes. The frontend module needs no build of its own.

[The launch walked through with screenshots](https://github.com/mherman22/openmrs-distro-smartonfhir/blob/main/docs/ehr-launch.md)
— what a clinician sees, what happens on the wire, and why no second login appears.

## Issue I worked on

see https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/FM2-690

## Checklist: I completed these to help reviewers :)

- [x] My IDE is configured to follow the [**code style**](https://wiki.openmrs.org/display/docs/Java+Conventions) of this project.
- [x] I have **added tests** to cover my changes.
- [x] I ran `mvn clean install` right before creating this pull request and added all formatting changes to my commit.
- [x] All new and existing **tests passed**.
- [x] My pull request is **based on the latest changes** of the master branch.

nodes.body:
`getUserByUsername` returns null when the realm has no user by that name, and `setAuthenticatedUser(null)` is legal (the SPI documents null explicitly), so nothing fails on these two lines. It fails later: `AuthenticationProcessor` throws `AuthenticationFlowException(UNKNOWN_USER)` whenever the session reaches the end of the flow with no authenticated user, so the clinician lands on a generic error page. The branch a few lines up handles the same class of problem the other way, calling `context.attempted()` so the next alternative runs. Was that asymmetry deliberate? An OpenMRS user with no Keycloak counterpart looks like exactly the case where falling through to the password form is the graceful answer, and `writeContextNotes` has already run by then either way.

Separately, nothing in the test suite reaches `action()`, and this is the behaviour FM2-690 is largely about: the clinician now comes from the token's subject rather than the hard-coded `admin`. `SmartAudienceValidatorTest` shows the mocking involved is manageable. A test that a valid token resolves the named user, plus one for whichever answer you give above, would pin the change that matters most here.

Leftovers from the action token this method no longer builds: `clientId` here and `validityInSecs`/`absoluteExpirationInSecs` just above are never read now, and `buildUserNameToken` (line 187) has no caller, which leaves `Urls`, `Time`, `JWSBuilder`, `KeyWrapper`, `MacSignatureSignerContext`, `SignatureSignerContext`, `Algorithm`, `URL` and `MalformedURLException` imported for it alone. `java.util.Map` and the static `SMART_NOTE_PREFIX` import fell out of use when the claim loop moved into `writeContextNotes`.

`SmartLaunchAccessActionToken` and its handler are orphaned by the same change. Nothing constructs the token any more, so the handler stays registered for a type Keycloak can never be handed. UPGRADING.md section 5 still lists that handler as a live coupling to re-verify on a version bump, a paragraph above the note explaining that the EHR path deliberately avoids action tokens.

Nothing in FM2-690 asks for this, and it's the one file in the diff that isn't the port or its documentation. I'd take it, just on its own PR, so this one stays reviewable as the thing it is: 38 unrelated lines is cheap to check once and permanently in the way of anyone reading back over the Keycloak 26 change. README.md and UPGRADING.md I'd keep here, they document the port's own couplings.
